concepts.name: Sea Level Rise: Mechanisms and Differentiated Impacts
key_dimensions: Two distinct causes: thermal expansion of seawater vs. melting of land-based ice (glaciers/ice sheets) — UPSC trap: sea ice melting does NOT raise sea level
Differential vulnerability: small island developing states (SIDS) like Tuvalu, Maldives vs. delta regions like Sundarbans and Bangladesh
Distinction between mean sea level rise and extreme sea level events (storm surges, tidal flooding)
IPCC AR6 projections: 'low-likelihood but high-impact' scenarios of ice sheet collapse and multi-metre rise

concepts.name: Arctic Amplification and Polar Ice Dynamics
key_dimensions: Why the Arctic warms 2–4× faster than the global average — ice-albedo feedback mechanism
Distinction between Arctic sea ice (floating, does not raise sea level) and Greenland ice sheet (land-based, raises sea level)
Consequences for mid-latitude weather: jet stream weakening, 'Polar Vortex' disruptions, and extreme cold events in temperate zones
Geopolitical dimensions: opening of Arctic shipping routes (Northwest Passage) and resource competition — overlap with IR syllabus

concepts.name: Ocean Acidification: Chemistry, Thresholds, and Ecological Cascades
key_dimensions: Mechanism: CO₂ + H₂O → carbonic acid → reduction in pH (pre-industrial ~8.2 to current ~8.1 — logarithmic scale trap)
Impact on calcifying organisms: coral reefs, pteropods, oysters — aragonite saturation threshold as a tipping point
Distinction from ocean warming: two separate but synergistic stressors on marine ecosystems
Consequences for fisheries, food security, and Blue Economy — UPSC policy linkage

concepts.name: Coral Bleaching: Triggers, Frequency, and Recovery Windows
key_dimensions: Mechanism: thermal stress → expulsion of zooxanthellae → bleaching (bleaching ≠ death; recovery possible if stress is brief)
1°C above mean summer maximum for 4+ weeks as the standard bleaching threshold — El Niño compounding effect
Mass bleaching events on the Great Barrier Reef (2016, 2017, 2020, 2022) — shrinking recovery intervals
UPSC trap: coral bleaching is also triggered by cold water, pollution, and disease — not exclusively by warming

concepts.name: Permafrost Thaw and the Carbon-Climate Feedback Loop
key_dimensions: Permafrost stores ~1,700 Gt of organic carbon — nearly twice the current atmospheric CO₂ — scale comparison trap
Release pathways: slow aerobic decomposition (CO₂) vs. anaerobic waterlogged decomposition (CH₄ — 80× more potent over 20 years)
Thermokarst lakes and abrupt permafrost thaw as non-linear 'tipping points' distinct from gradual thaw
Infrastructure consequences: collapsing buildings, pipelines in Siberia and Alaska — socioeconomic dimension

concepts.name: Glacial Retreat and Cryosphere-Linked Water Security
key_dimensions: Glacier as a 'water tower': seasonal buffering role vs. permanent ice loss — 'peak water' concept (initial increase then sharp decline in meltwater)
Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) glaciers: 'Third Pole' — source for 10 major Asian river systems affecting 2 billion people
Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs): mechanism, risk to downstream communities, recent Uttarakhand and Pakistan events
UPSC trap: not all glaciers are retreating at the same rate — Karakoram Anomaly (some glaciers advancing due to unique precipitation patterns)

concepts.name: Intensification of the Hydrological Cycle: Floods, Droughts, and Precipitation Shifts
key_dimensions: Thermodynamic basis: Clausius-Clapeyron relation — ~7% increase in atmospheric moisture per 1°C warming → more intense precipitation
'Wet gets wetter, dry gets drier' paradigm and its exceptions — monsoon regions show non-linear responses
Simultaneous increase in both flood frequency AND drought severity — not mutually exclusive (UPSC trap)
India-specific: intensification of extreme rainfall events, erratic monsoon onset, and longer dry spells within the monsoon season

concepts.name: Tropical Cyclone Intensification Under Global Warming
key_dimensions: Distinction: global warming may not increase the total NUMBER of cyclones but increases the proportion of Category 4–5 cyclones
Rapid intensification (RI) events: >35 knots wind speed increase in 24 hours — warming makes RI more likely and harder to forecast
Poleward migration of cyclone peak intensity — new regions like Arabian Sea becoming more cyclogenically active
UPSC trap: warming may suppress cyclones in some basins (e.g., increased wind shear in North Atlantic) — regional variability is key

concepts.name: Heat Waves: Definition, Thresholds, and Human Health Impacts
key_dimensions: IMD definition of heat wave vs. WHO definition — different thresholds create confusion in data comparison (UPSC trap)
Wet-bulb temperature (WBT) of 35°C as the survivability threshold — why humidity matters more than dry temperature alone
Heat stress on labour productivity: ILO estimates of lost work hours — economic cost quantification
Disproportionate impact on urban populations (Urban Heat Island effect) and vulnerable groups — climate justice dimension

concepts.name: Urban Heat Island (UHI) Effect: Interaction with Global Warming
key_dimensions: Mechanism: dark surfaces, reduced vegetation, waste heat from human activity — distinct from but amplified by global warming
UHI can add 1–3°C above regional warming — cities experience warming faster than rural areas
Policy responses: cool roofs, green roofs, urban forests — distinction between mitigation (reducing GHGs) and adaptation (managing heat)
UPSC overlap: UHI is relevant to Smart Cities Mission, urban planning, and disaster management syllabus

concepts.name: Shifting Agricultural Zones and Food Security Implications
key_dimensions: CO₂ fertilization effect: higher CO₂ boosts some C3 crops (wheat, rice) but co-occurring stressors (heat, drought) negate gains — UPSC trap
Crop yield projections: IPCC finding of 2–6% decline per decade for major cereals beyond 1.5°C for tropical regions
Poleward and altitudinal shift of cultivation zones — opportunity for some high-latitude nations vs. loss for tropical countries
India-specific: impact on Kharif crops (heat stress during grain filling), wheat in Indo-Gangetic Plain, and marine fisheries

concepts.name: Vector-Borne and Climate-Sensitive Disease Dynamics
key_dimensions: Expansion of Anopheles mosquito range with warming — malaria moving to higher altitudes (Ethiopian and Andean highlands)
Distinction: warming expands geographic range of vectors but higher temperatures can also reduce vector survival (non-linear relationship)
Cholera and waterborne diseases linked to warming sea surface temperatures (Vibrio cholerae blooms) and extreme rainfall events
UPSC trap: climate change is an 'amplifier' of disease burden, not the sole determinant — socioeconomic factors (sanitation, healthcare) interact

concepts.name: Biodiversity Loss and Species Range Shifts: 'Fingerprint' of Climate Change
key_dimensions: Three observable fingerprints: poleward range shifts, upward altitudinal migration, and phenological changes (earlier spring events)
Phenology mismatch: 'trophic asynchrony' — e.g., insect emergence decoupled from bird migration or flower blooming
IPCC finding: ~1 million species at risk — distinction between 'at risk' (trajectory) and 'extinct' (UPSC precision trap)
Coral reef systems: disproportionate biodiversity value (~25% of marine species) vs. coverage (~1% of ocean floor)

concepts.name: Climate Change and Human Displacement: 'Climate Refugees' and Legal Gaps
key_dimensions: UPSC trap: 'climate refugee' has NO legal recognition under the 1951 Refugee Convention — displaced persons have no international protection
Internal displacement vs. cross-border migration — World Bank estimates 216 million internal climate migrants by 2050
Slow-onset events (sea level rise, desertification) vs. sudden-onset events (floods, cyclones) as different drivers of migration
Groundbreaking case: Teitiota v. New Zealand (UN Human Rights Committee, 2020) — first recognition that returning someone to climate-threatened home could violate right to life

concepts.name: Ocean Deoxygenation and Dead Zones
key_dimensions: Mechanism: warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen + increased stratification prevents oxygen-rich surface water from mixing downward
Distinction between open-ocean deoxygenation (driven by warming) and coastal dead zones (driven primarily by nutrient runoff/eutrophication) — UPSC trap
Impacts on fish habitat compression: 'oxygen minimum zones' expanding and forcing fish toward surface — increases fishing pressure
Interaction with acidification and warming: 'triple threat' to marine ecosystems — synergistic vs. additive effects

concepts.name: Tipping Points and Non-Linear Climate Thresholds
key_dimensions: Definition: threshold beyond which a system self-perpetuates change independent of further forcing — distinct from gradual linear change
Key tipping elements: West Antarctic Ice Sheet, Amazon dieback, Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) slowdown, permafrost carbon bomb
AMOC slowdown: UPSC-relevant because it paradoxically causes cooling in Northwest Europe despite global warming — counterintuitive trap
Cascading tipping points: 'tipping cascade' concept — one tipping point triggering another (Potsdam Institute research, 2018)

concepts.name: Differential Vulnerability and Climate Justice: Developed vs. Developing Nations
key_dimensions: Historical emissions responsibility vs. current vulnerability — least developed countries (LDCs) contribute <1% of global emissions but face highest risks
IPCC AR6 'Reason for Concern' framework: risks to unique systems, extreme events, distribution of impacts, aggregate damages, large-scale singular events
Loss and Damage: distinct from mitigation (preventing) and adaptation (adjusting) — COP27 breakthrough: establishment of Loss and Damage fund
UPSC trap: 'common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities' (CBDR-RC) — 'common' refers to shared responsibility, 'differentiated' to historical burden

concepts.name: Impact on Indian Monsoon System and Regional Precipitation Patterns
key_dimensions: Aerosol masking effect: particulate pollution (especially over South Asia) has historically suppressed monsoon rainfall — complex interaction with greenhouse warming
Differential warming of land vs. sea affects land-sea thermal contrast — the fundamental driver of monsoon circulation
Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) and El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) teleconnections becoming more variable under warming — monsoon prediction challenge
UPSC trap: global warming's effect on Indian monsoon is NOT straightforwardly positive or negative — it increases variability and extremes while total annual rainfall changes remain uncertain

concepts.name: Wildfire Regime Shifts Under Climate Change
key_dimensions: Fire weather: combination of heat, drought, low humidity, and wind — all amplified by warming ('fire weather season' lengthening globally)
Distinction between fire suppression policy failures and climate change as drivers — UPSC analytical precision required
Carbon feedback: boreal forest and peatland fires release stored carbon, creating positive feedback loop — 'zombie fires' (underground peat fires persisting through winter)
India relevance: increasing forest fires in Northeast India, Uttarakhand — link to forest fire management policy and Forest Survey of India reports

concepts.name: Economic Costs of Climate Change: Aggregate Damage Functions and Inequality
key_dimensions: Stern Review (2006) vs. Nordhaus (2018 Nobel Prize): divergence on discount rate and intergenerational equity — high discount rate minimises future damages
Non-market damages: loss of biodiversity, cultural heritage, human health — difficult to monetise but excluded from standard GDP-based models
Unequal distribution: Burke et al. finding that warming benefits cold high-income countries while harming hot low-income countries — widening global inequality
UPSC policy linkage: economic cost estimates underpin carbon pricing, climate finance ($100 billion pledge), and Loss and Damage negotiations
